newsitem.title: UK: GDR REPORT-India GDRs sag on holiday, Taiwan stars.
newsitem.headline: GDR REPORT-India GDRs sag on holiday, Taiwan stars.

text.p: Indian GDRs limped into the weekend with little panache due to an Indian market holiday, leaving Taiwanese paper to steal the market limelight, dealers said.
"Taiwan continued very strong. It's had a very good run," said one trader at a major brokerage here after the Taipei stock market ended at its highest level in nearly seven years.
Investor fervour was prompted in part by signs the economy is on the mend after news last month it grew at a stronger than expected rate in the fourth quarter of last year.
The enthusiasm shows no sign of abating as it shrugs off the central bank's ambivalence over the stock market rally and discounts less positive economic signals.
The Capel Taiwan GDR Index ended 1.72 points, or 1.60 percent higher at 109.42, with a premium of 0.20 percent over the local market.
The Taiwan Weighted Index rose 81.68 point, or 1.01 percent, to end at 8,162.68.
With Indian stock markets closed for a Hindu festival, players were looking ahead to a session of consolidation on Monday.
The HSBC James Capel Indian GDR index JCEAI closed down 2.39 points, or 3.12 percent, at 74.08 points, with the premium over the local market at 11.74 percent.
The Capel Korea GDR Index ended down 0.24 points, or 0.40 percent at 59.33 points, a premium of 39.76 percent.
The Korea Composite Index ended 3.11 points firmer at 681.22 after buying of small individual stocks, and despite fizzling interest from general investors.
